comments.author: @leslieviljoen
comments.text:
I believe Sam Altman is genuine - but since Meta gave the world a foundation to build on, the big companies are going to soon lose the lead. Open models based on LLaMA have been rapidly improving and who can stop them overtaking GPT4? Not just in training but also execution. Yesterday I ran Vicuna in Chrome on my very average GPU using WebGPU - with usable performance. Will we need massive GPU farms to make better models in the future? I doubt it. And even if LLaMA hadn't been released, I expect open source would have gotten there, it would just have taken a bit longer.

My hope is that LLM"s can't go dramatically beyond human cognitive capabilities for some reason, because I'm not sure alignment is possible without highly capable legibility, and people always develop capabilities first.

Even if this crazy hope comes true, something better than LLM's seems likely within a decade or two anyway, and then once again we'll develop capabilities before legibility. Humans just don't learn without making mistakes and unfortunately this time our first mistake is going to be our last.
